title: How do we read a lakh group with two digits?
description: The video writes two more big numbers in words, where the lakh group has two digits and one group ends in zeros. Keeko raises a hand, thinking that seventy lakh can be read as seven zero lakh.
teaching_notes: One idea: a group is read as one number, whatever its digits, and then given its place name. Ask the class to read each group on its own before adding lakh or thousand. Watch for students who read the digits of a group one at a time.

video_script.why: The child can split a big number at its commas and read each group with its place name.
video_script.substitution: Each group is read as one number and then given its place name; a group of zeros is not said.
video_script.anchor: Write the numbers 27,30,000 and 70,53,138 in words
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the two digits of the lakh group one at a time. Seven zero lakh says nothing about the number seventy.
video_script.payoff_line: The second number is seventy lakh fifty three thousand one hundred thirty eight

final_answer.spoken: seventy lakh fifty three thousand one hundred thirty eight

hold_back: seventy lakh fifty three thousand one hundred thirty eight
never_show: a number with a crore group
maths_rules: (c) 27,30,000: 27 lakh, 30 thousand, 000 not said; twenty seven lakh thirty thousand
(d) 70,53,138: 70 lakh, 53 thousand, 138; seventy lakh fifty three thousand one hundred thirty eight
the slip: 70 read digit by digit as seven zero lakh
video_script.design: One idea: each group is read as one number, then given its place name. Wrong idea: Keeko reads seventy digit by digit. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.
